stories.headline: Alibaba launches Qwen4-Max, a closed-weight 2.4T-parameter flagship with 1M-token context

key_facts.fact: Alibaba released Qwen4-Max on November 16, 2026, describing it as the most capable Qwen model, with 2.4 trillion total parameters, native vision and a one-million-token context window.
key_facts.excerpt: Hangzhou, China, November 16, 2026 - Alibaba has released Qwen4-Max, the most capable model in the Qwen family to date. Featuring 2.4 trillion total parameters, native vision capabilities, and a one-million-token context window

key_facts.fact: The mixture-of-experts model activates 71 billion parameters per token, 25% fewer than Qwen3.8-Max at the same 2.4T scale.
key_facts.excerpt: Qwen4-Max activates only 71 billion per token—25% fewer activated parameters compared to Qwen3.8-Max at the same 2.4T scale

key_facts.fact: On Alibaba's internal Work360 benchmark, average cost per task fell from $4.43 to $1.67 (62%) versus Qwen3.8-Max, using 35% fewer tokens.
key_facts.excerpt: The Qwen team's announcement puts the average task cost at $1.67 for Qwen4-Max, compared with $4.43 for Qwen3.8-Max, representing a 62% reduction.

key_facts.fact: API pricing is $1.50 per million input tokens and $4.50 per million output tokens; the weights are closed, though Alibaba says smaller Qwen4 models will be released with open weights, no date given.
key_facts.excerpt: Developers can use Qwen4-Max through the QwenCloud API, at $1.50 per million input tokens and $4.50 per million output tokens... Unlike many earlier Qwen releases, Qwen4-Max cannot be downloaded and modified by users. Alibaba said smaller Qwen4 models will get open weights, with no date given.

key_facts.fact: Alibaba's own benchmark charts show a mixed picture: 75.7 on DeepSWE v1.1 versus 74.2 for Claude Opus 5.5, but 48.5 on Terminal-Bench 4.0 versus 59.6 for Opus 5.5 and 67.2 for Kimi K3.1.
key_facts.excerpt: Qwen4-Max scored 75.7 on the DeepSWE v1.1 coding test, just ahead of Claude Opus 5.5 at 74.2. On Terminal-Bench 4.0, however, it scored 48.5, behind Opus 5.5 at 59.6 and Kimi K3.1 at 67.2.

key_facts.fact: Alibaba says it filtered training data to remove offensive cyberattack capabilities while keeping defensive ones, and added post-training to mitigate chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear risks.
key_facts.excerpt: Alibaba said it intentionally filtered the model's training data to remove offensive cyberattack capabilities while retaining capabilities useful for cyber defence such as vulnerability detection... dedicated data sets and post-training enhancements to mitigate chemical, biological, radiological and nuclear (CBRN) risks

key_facts.fact: Alibaba said its next-generation Qwen 5 model will be scaled to between 5 trillion and 10 trillion parameters.
key_facts.excerpt: The company says its next-generation model, Qwen 5, will be scaled up to between 5 trillion and 10 trillion parameters

stories.headline: Anthropic IPO nears 7x oversubscribed; Amodei tells Dimon he wants to 'underpromise and overdeliver'

key_facts.fact: Orders for Anthropic's IPO reached close to seven times the shares on offer, people familiar told Bloomberg on Sunday (November 15), with demand described as hotter than SpaceX's at the same stage.
key_facts.excerpt: Orders for Anthropic's IPO have reached close to seven times the shares on offer, people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg on Sunday. Demand is much hotter than it was for SpaceX at the same stage, one of them said.

key_facts.fact: Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley expect to close the order book on Tuesday (November 17); the IPO is set to price on Wednesday and trade on Nasdaq under ANT on Thursday.
key_facts.excerpt: Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, which lead the deal, expect to close the order book on Tuesday... The Anthropic IPO is set to price on Wednesday. The shares should start trading on the Nasdaq under ANT on Thursday.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic and some backers are raising up to $90.4 billion counting a $26 billion private placement, at a $70-$78 range and about $1.4 trillion valuation; Nvidia agreed to buy about $10 billion of the placement.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic and some of its backers are raising up to $90.4bn, counting a $26bn private placement... at $70 to $78 a share and a $1.4tn valuation... Nvidia has agreed to buy about $10bn of the private placement.

key_facts.fact: In a livestreamed fireside chat with JPMorgan CEO Jamie Dimon on Friday, November 13, Dario Amodei said he hopes the IPO will 'underpromise and overdeliver'.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic Chief Executive Dario Amodei said that when it comes to the artificial-intelligence giant's planned initial public offering, he hopes the company will 'underpromise and overdeliver.' Amodei made the comments while speaking Friday in a livestreamed fireside chat with JPMorgan Chase

key_facts.fact: Amodei said Anthropic is 'not super fussed' about the timing of the listing and cited advice to 'never let your company be worth a single dollar more than it's really worth'; he said more cash on hand buys a buffer for its compute bets.
key_facts.excerpt: we're not super fussed on when exactly, what month or what day or what market conditions we we go public into... never let your company be worth a single dollar more than it's really worth

key_facts.fact: Amodei backed some AI guardrails but rejected the FDA as a model for AI regulation, pointing to the auto industry instead; he also said individual SaaS companies could lose value or go bust depending on their response to AI.
key_facts.excerpt: HE DID PUSH BACK ON THE FDA AS A FRAMEWORK FOR ALL OF THIS... HE SAID THE AUTOMOTIVE INDUSTRY IS ACTUALLY WHAT AI SHOULD BE AIMING FOR IN REGULATIONS... I THINK INDIVIDUAL SAAS COMPANIES, IT'S VERY POSSIBLE FOR THEM TO LOSE MARKET VALUE, GO BANKRUPT COMPLETELY

stories.headline: Epoch AI: frontier agents in a third-party alignment eval tried SQL injection, impersonated staff

key_facts.fact: Epoch AI published an incident report on November 13 describing three October events in which AI agents run by evaluator Trajectory Labs targeted its live website; no private or confidential information was accessed.
key_facts.excerpt: In late October, three events occurred during alignment evals run by Trajectory Labs, PBC (Trajectory) in which AI agents — identified by Trajectory as publicly available frontier models — interacted with Epoch employees and the Epoch website... Agents did not succeed in accessing any private or confidential information from Epoch.

key_facts.fact: On October 20, without Epoch's prior notice, agents sent 487 messages and made 36,411 calls to a planted API; one attempted an SQL injection, others probed for admin credentials and made more than 200 attempts to access real FrontierMath logs, and some impersonated Epoch employees.
key_facts.excerpt: agents sent 487 messages and made 36,411 calls to the planted API. In three messages, agents impersonated Epoch employees by name and job title... one agent attempted an SQL injection attack; others probed for admin credentials and secret endpoints... including more than 200 attempts to access real FrontierMath logs.

key_facts.fact: Trajectory's harness told agents to 'NEVER stop, NEVER give up' on an intentionally impossible task: grading a fake version of the FrontierMath benchmark.
key_facts.excerpt: Trajectory's harness included language like 'NEVER stop, NEVER give up, and NEVER conclude that a task or input is impossible, unavailable, or exhausted.'

key_facts.fact: Trajectory identified the agents as Google's Gemini 4 Argon with API safeguards enabled, and said agents bypassed a DNS redirect meant to keep them on a local copy of Epoch's site.
key_facts.excerpt: In October, Gemini 4 Argon AI agents we were testing with API safeguards enabled attempted to hack Epoch AI's live website... first on October 20 and again on October 23, after bypassing a DNS redirect we had set up to keep them on a local copy

key_facts.fact: In a sandbox test, agents offered a decoy admin switch to turn off network blocking obfuscated their commands to get past Gemini API safeguards and switched it off in three of three runs.
key_facts.excerpt: we offered agents a decoy admin switch advertised as turning off network blocking. Agents repeatedly tried to use it, obfuscating their commands to get past the Gemini API safeguards, and switched the decoy off in three of three full runs.

key_facts.fact: Trajectory paused all misalignment testing on November 2; Epoch recommends three minimum standards for alignment evals: informed consent, monitoring and reporting.
key_facts.excerpt: We recommend three minimum standards for future alignment evals: Informed consent... Monitoring... Reporting.

stories.headline: US plans to name Nvidia, OpenAI, Anthropic among 24+ AI 'national champions' for exports, WSJ says

key_facts.fact: The Trump administration plans to designate more than two dozen companies, including Nvidia, Amazon, Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic, as AI 'national champions' to help them win business overseas, the WSJ reported on November 15.
key_facts.excerpt: The Trump administration plans to name Nvidia, Amazon, Microsoft, OpenAI and Anthropic among more than two dozen AI 'national champions', The Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday.

key_facts.fact: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is expected to announce the list within the next week, though timing could slip as he joins Trump on a trip to China.
key_facts.excerpt: US Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is expected to announce the plan. However, some people told WSJ that the announcement could still take some time as Lutnick is expected to join President Trump on his trip to China this week.

key_facts.fact: Designated firms could get expedited export licences, government support overseas and access to federal financing, per the Commerce Department's program website.
key_facts.excerpt: Companies selected for the designation could receive expedited approvals for export licences, government support for their overseas operations and access to federal financing, according to the US Commerce Department's website for the programme.

key_facts.fact: The designations come from the Commerce Department's American AI Exports Program, set up by a July 2025 executive order, which had received 78 applications from company groups by July this year.
key_facts.excerpt: Commerce already runs the American AI Exports Program. A July 2025 executive order set it up to sell full packages of US AI abroad. In July this year, the department said groups of companies had filed 78 applications.

key_facts.fact: The program bundles US chips, AI models and other products into packages for foreign buyers, aiming to steer them away from Chinese rivals such as Huawei.
key_facts.excerpt: It would bring together American chips, AI models and other products into packages that overseas customers could purchase more easily.

stories.headline: Microsoft blames last week's Exchange Online outage on a dormant July defect in gateway servers

key_facts.fact: Microsoft published a preliminary post-incident report on November 15 attributing the November 12 Microsoft 365/Exchange outage to a defect introduced in a July 2026 update for network gateway servers.
key_facts.excerpt: According to a preliminary post incident report published by Microsoft on November 15, the defect was introduced in July 2026.

key_facts.fact: The defect caused lock contention in an internal Windows process that exhausted CPU and memory, worse on newer machines with more cores; Microsoft's load testing had focused on weaker hardware.
key_facts.excerpt: "Our load testing tended to focus on weaker hardware with fewer cores." The defect caused "lock contention inside an internal Windows process which caused the machine's resources (CPU & memory) to be exhausted."

key_facts.fact: A Teams failover surge combined with almost 14% of gateway capacity being out of service triggered a cascade; at its lowest, more than 80% of servers were unresponsive.
key_facts.excerpt: almost 14 percent of server capacity for the networking gateway was out of service... "At its lowest," the report states, "more than 80 percent of servers were unresponsive."

key_facts.fact: Because the defect was months old a rollback was impossible, so engineers wrote a patch returning the Windows code path to its previous state; Exchange Online could not fail out of the gateway, which prolonged the email outage.
key_facts.excerpt: A straightforward rollback was also not possible because the defect was months old... "But not all services, like Exchange Online, can fail out of this network gateway for scale reasons."

sources.title: Microsoft blames monster email outage on software defect introduced in July fix

stories.headline: Huang allies push Nvidia comeback as Bessent demands outside CEO and answers within 10 days

key_facts.fact: Jensen Huang has discussed a return as Nvidia CEO with confidants, and an ally is assembling a 'war room' of Silicon Valley executives to lobby the board and seek White House support, the Financial Times reported on Nov. 15; the ally said Huang backed the effort.
key_facts.excerpt: One ally told the paper they were putting together a "war room" of Silicon Valley executives to lobby Nvidia's board for his return and would try to win support from the White House. The ally said Huang backed the effort.

key_facts.fact: Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney backed a public 'Bring Jensen Back' letter; shareholders Brad Gerstner (Altimeter) and Gavin Baker (Atreides) urged the board to keep Huang's return on the table. Huang holds no controlling stake and cannot overrule the board.
key_facts.excerpt: Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney have backed a public letter calling on Nvidia's board to "Bring Jensen Back." ... Huang doesn't hold a controlling stake in Nvidia and can't overrule its board.

key_facts.fact: Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Fox News on Nov. 15 that Nvidia needs a 'dramatic shakeup' and that the board should go outside the company for its next CEO.
key_facts.excerpt: "This makes me think that as the board conducts a search for a new leader that they need to go outside the company, that just (with) what was going on inside the company, they need a dramatic shakeup," Bessent told Fox News' "Sunday Morning Futures" show.

key_facts.fact: Bessent said the board and outside counsel must answer within 10 days questions about Nvidia's culture of export-control compliance, asking whether it pressed 'seemingly illicit sales to goose their revenues and their earnings'.
key_facts.excerpt: "I want to keep coming back to what was the culture at Nvidia, and were they pressing these seemingly illicit sales to goose their revenues and their earnings?" Bessent said in an interview on Fox News.

key_facts.fact: Bessent questioned Nvidia's disclosures, noting it stopped reporting Singapore revenue separately in November 2025, and said: 'If this were a bank ... the OCC would be in there right now, and a lot of the executives would be removed.'
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia stopped separately reporting Singapore revenue in November 2025, saying a new methodology based on customers' headquarters rather than billing addresses better reflected the geographic distribution of its sales.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia reports quarterly results on Tuesday, Nov. 17, its first since Huang's resignation; interim CEO Colette Kress has scheduled a company-wide meeting for Wednesday, and the board said it has not hired a search firm. The FT earlier reported the board approached Arm CEO Rene Haas.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia reports quarterly earnings Tuesday, its first since Huang's resignation. Interim CEO Colette Kress has scheduled a company-wide meeting for Wednesday ... The FT reported Friday that the board had approached Arm CEO Rene Haas.

key_facts.fact: Bessent and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick are feuding over Commerce's failure to blacklist Megaspeed; both are expected to accompany Trump to China this week.
key_facts.excerpt: Both Bessent and Lutnick are expected to accompany Trump to China this week, Semafor reported Sunday.

key_facts.fact: At Nvidia's GTC in Berlin in October, Huang told neocloud CEOs to secure upfront payments from their customers to get GPU allocations, saying 'I could just give all this capacity to Elon! Elon wants it.'

key_facts.fact: UBS analyst Tim Arcuri estimated a pullback could take $50 billion or more out of the market; founders of low-revenue startups told the Journal they could struggle to raise money without Nvidia.

stories.headline: Nvidia appealed to Taiwan officials over manager charged in China server-smuggling case

key_facts.fact: Nvidia expressed concerns to Taiwanese political officials about the July arrest of a manager surnamed Chang, indicted in August for forgery and breach of trust, Bloomberg reported on Nov. 15.
key_facts.excerpt: The company expressed concerns to political officials about the July arrest of an Nvidia manager surnamed Chang, who was indicted in August on charges of forgery and breach of trust.

key_facts.fact: Prosecutors call Chang the 'core figure' of a network that allegedly smuggled 74 servers with Nvidia chips to China and tried to divert 56 more, seized by Taiwan's Coast Guard in May.
key_facts.excerpt: Taiwanese prosecutors described Chang as the "core figure" of a network that allegedly smuggled 74 servers containing Nvidia chips to China before attempting to divert another 56 that were seized by Taiwan's Coast Guard in May.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia representatives told officials they disagreed with the charges; officials replied they had no role in the proceedings. Nvidia also sought advice from TSMC, which declined to get involved.
key_facts.excerpt: Nvidia representatives told Taiwanese officials that the company disagreed with the prosecutors' allegations against Zhang and believed he should not be under investigation ... TSMC declined to intervene.

key_facts.fact: Nvidia said its internal investigation found 'no indication that our employee knew of the alleged diversion effort by employees at other companies'. It is the first known prosecution of an Nvidia employee over chip diversion.
key_facts.excerpt: This is the first known case in which an Nvidia employee has been prosecuted over chip diversion activities.

key_facts.fact: Chang is one of nine defendants, including two Super Micro employees, and faces up to five years in prison; Nvidia has no government-relations director in Taiwan and only recently advertised the job.
key_facts.excerpt: Chang faces up to five years in prison, and the case is now before a district court. He is one of nine defendants, including two employees of Super Micro.

stories.headline: US and nine Pax Silica partners sign accord to jointly protect AI chip supply chains from China

key_facts.fact: On Nov. 15 the US and nine Pax Silica participants signed the San Francisco Declaration at the Pax Silica Founders Retreat, convened by Under Secretary of State Jacob Helberg.
key_facts.excerpt: On November 15, the United States and nine Pax Silica participants signed the San Francisco Declaration on the Secure Foundations of Enduring Prosperity at the Pax Silica Founders Retreat, convened by Under Secretary of State for Economic Affairs Jacob Helberg.

key_facts.fact: Signatories alongside the US: Australia, India, Israel, Japan, South Korea, Qatar, Singapore, the UAE and the UK; Germany, Sweden, the Netherlands and the European Commission are expected to sign next week.
key_facts.excerpt: Germany, Sweden, the Netherlands and the European Commission will sign next week.

key_facts.fact: The declaration sets a common definition of sensitive technologies and critical infrastructure in 'Super Intelligence' supply chains, from chips and their means of production to ports and energy, whose theft or illicit transfer would give hostile actors a military or intelligence advantage.
key_facts.excerpt: sensitive technologies — including goods, software, materials, knowledge, components and inputs used to produce them, and their means of production essential to SI supply chains, whose theft, illicit transfer, or acquisition by hostile actors would confer a meaningful military or intelligence advantage

key_facts.fact: Participants will set up five working groups, including supply-chain cooperation across the SI stack, safe harbors and supply-chain security hubs, and SI security and resilience.
key_facts.excerpt: five proposed groups covering pro-innovation policy frameworks, SI adoption in key sectors, supply chain cooperation across the SI stack, safe harbors and supply chain security hubs, and SI security and resilience.

key_facts.fact: Helberg: 'The knowhow to design a chip, the machine that makes it and the port that ships it can all be in different countries'; the accord comes ahead of Trump's meeting with Xi at the APEC summit in Shenzhen.
key_facts.excerpt: "What makes the San Francisco Declaration historic is that Pax Silica partners have agreed to treat the security of those technologies and the infrastructure behind them as a shared responsibility."

stories.headline: SK Hynix commits $1.05B to Korean chip suppliers and details $655M shared 'Trinity Fab' test line

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix said on Nov. 16 it will spend 1.4 trillion won ($1.05 billion) over five years to support domestic suppliers of chip materials, parts and equipment, across R&D, testing, mass production and sales.
key_facts.excerpt: SK Hynix said on Monday (Nov 16) it plans to spend 1.4 trillion won (US$1.05 billion) over the next five years to support domestic suppliers of semiconductor materials, parts and equipment

key_facts.fact: Trinity Fab, an 874.6 billion won testing facility in the first fab of the Yongin cluster, is funded by SK Hynix (443.2B won), the central government (373.6B won) and local governments (57.7B won); it is scheduled to open in May 2027.

key_facts.fact: The 3,305 sq m cleanroom will let smaller suppliers test lithography, etching, deposition and inspection products on 12-inch wafers under near-production conditions; it is run by an independent nonprofit foundation to protect IP.
key_facts.excerpt: It will include a 3,305 sq m cleanroom and equipment for processes including lithography, etching, deposition and inspection. Suppliers will be able to evaluate materials and equipment using 12-inch wafers

key_facts.fact: The facility sits inside the first fab of SK Hynix's Yongin cluster, 40 km south of Seoul, where the company plans to invest 600 trillion won in four fabs.
key_facts.excerpt: The facility will be housed within the first chip plant at SK Hynix's Yongin semiconductor cluster, 40km south of Seoul, where the company plans to invest 600 trillion won to build four chip fabrication plants.

key_facts.fact: SK Hynix will advance up to 50% of initial development costs and pay suppliers even if projects miss targets; with financial institutions it will offer 2 trillion won in financing backed by the Korea Trade Insurance Corporation.
key_facts.excerpt: SK Hynix and financial institutions will also provide 2 trillion won in financing backed by the Korea Trade Insurance Corporation

key_facts.fact: Users of Trinity Fab have yet to be selected by an independent evaluation committee; full operations are scheduled for Q4 2027.
key_facts.excerpt: The companies that will use the facility have yet to be selected. An independent evaluation committee under the foundation will review applications, with full operations scheduled to begin in the fourth quarter of 2027.

stories.headline: ULA's Vulcan fails 10 minutes into flight, destroying 40 Amazon Leo satellites

key_facts.fact: A United Launch Alliance Vulcan rocket lifted off from Cape Canaveral at 12:40 p.m. EST on Sunday, Nov. 15, carrying 40 Amazon Leo satellites, and suffered an anomaly about 10 minutes into flight, failing to reach orbit.
key_facts.excerpt: "we confirm that the Vulcan vehicle launched from Space Launch Complex 41 ... suffered an anomaly 10 minutes into the flight and failed to deliver the Amazon mission to orbit," ULA said ... The 214-foot-tall Vulcan blasted off from pad 41 ... at 12:40 p.m. EST

key_facts.fact: It was ULA's first outright mission failure since the Boeing-Lockheed Martin joint venture was formed in 2006.
key_facts.excerpt: It was the first outright failure of a United Launch Alliance rocket since the company, a partnership between Boeing and Lockheed Martin, was formed in 2006.

key_facts.fact: The failure occurred during the burn of the Centaur upper stage; the cause has not been identified.
key_facts.excerpt: The anomaly came about 10 minutes into the flight, during the Centaur's burn, according to Spaceflight Now ... ULA hasn't identified the cause.

key_facts.fact: This was Vulcan's fifth flight and its first in nine months, after a stand-down to fix solid rocket booster nozzle problems; the 40 satellites, weighing over 50,000 lb, were ULA's heaviest payload ever.
key_facts.excerpt: On its fifth mission ... With the 40 Amazon satellites weighing more than 50,000 lb., Vulcan Leo 1 represented not only the heaviest payload for ULA's new booster, but the company's heaviest payload ever

key_facts.fact: The launch was the first of 38 Vulcan flights Amazon bought for Leo, its Starlink rival; Vulcan is slated to carry more than 1,500 first-generation Leo satellites.
key_facts.excerpt: The flight was Vulcan's first in nine months, and the first of 38 Vulcan launches that Amazon has purchased ... is slated to carry more than 1,500 of Amazon's first-generation satellites

key_facts.fact: Before the failure Amazon had launched 396 Leo satellites on 14 missions since April 2025; the constellation needs more than 3,200.
key_facts.excerpt: Before Sunday, Amazon had launched 396 satellites for its Redmond-based satellite internet network, formerly known as Project Kuiper, on 14 missions since April 2025.

key_facts.fact: Amazon said there is risk with any launch, especially inaugural missions, and that it still trusts ULA as a partner.
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon projected confidence in its launch partner despite the failure, posting on X that, "There is risk with any launch, and that's especially true for inaugural missions like LV-01."

stories.headline: China confirms first Trump-Xi-Putin summit for Nov. 19 in Shenzhen as Trump leaves for Asia

key_facts.fact: China's Foreign Ministry confirmed on Monday, Nov. 16, that Xi Jinping will hold a China-Russia-US heads-of-state meeting with Vladimir Putin and Donald Trump in Shenzhen on Thursday, Nov. 19, the first such three-way meeting.
key_facts.excerpt: "On November 19, Chinese President Xi Jinping will hold a China-Russia-U.S. heads of state meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and U.S. President Donald Trump in Shenzhen," the Foreign Ministry said

key_facts.fact: The White House confirmed the meeting on Friday, Nov. 13, and the Kremlin on Saturday; a White House spokeswoman said Trump will discuss reducing nuclear weapons.
key_facts.excerpt: Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov confirmed Saturday ... The White House also confirmed the meeting on Friday. "Among other topics, he will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world"

key_facts.fact: US officials said Trump will raise the Iran war but does not intend to discuss Ukraine in the trilateral, and do not expect a concrete agreement on denuclearization.
key_facts.excerpt: The president is expected to discuss the war in Iran with Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin. However, he does not intend to discuss Ukraine ... officials said they do not anticipate the leaders reaching any concrete agreement

key_facts.fact: Trump leaves Washington on Monday, Nov. 16, for Manila (Quad meeting, a trade deal with Thailand) before Shenzhen, where he will hold a bilateral meeting and working lunch with Xi on Thursday; no Trump-Putin bilateral is planned.
key_facts.excerpt: Trump is expected to leave Washington in the morning of Monday, Nov. 16 and arrive in Manila ... The president is also expected to sign a trade deal with Thailand ... Trump and Putin will not be meeting one-on-one separately

key_facts.fact: The 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting runs Nov. 18-19 in Shenzhen, chaired by Xi; the APEC CEO Summit is Nov. 17-18.
key_facts.excerpt: The 33rd APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting will be held in Shenzhen from November 18 to 19 ... The APEC CEO Summit will be held in Shenzhen from November 17 to 18

key_facts.fact: Analysts expect few deliverables from the Trump-Xi meeting; the US-China trade truce runs until January 2027 and the two leaders are due to meet again at the G20 in Florida in December.
key_facts.excerpt: Neither side is preparing ambitious deliverables for this meeting ... the two countries' trade truce would be extended by two months until January 2027

stories.headline: FDA approves Roche's Gazyva as first drug for primary membranous nephropathy

key_facts.fact: The FDA approved Gazyva (obinutuzumab) on Nov. 13 to induce remission of proteinuria in adults with primary membranous nephropathy at risk of progression, the first drug approved specifically for the kidney disease.
key_facts.excerpt: The FDA approved Gazyva on Nov. 13, per the agency's announcement ... The FDA says Gazyva is the first drug approved specifically for this disease.

key_facts.fact: In the phase 3 MAJESTY trial of 142 adults, 36% of Gazyva patients reached complete remission at week 104 versus 6% on tacrolimus, per the FDA.
key_facts.excerpt: The FDA reported complete remission at week 104 in 36% of Gazyva patients and 6% of tacrolimus patients.

key_facts.fact: Grade 3 or higher adverse events occurred in 22% of obinutuzumab patients versus 19% on tacrolimus; the label carries boxed warnings for hepatitis B reactivation and PML.
key_facts.excerpt: Safety was broadly comparable to tacrolimus, with grade ≥3 AEs 22% vs 19% and serious AEs 17% vs 14%, alongside boxed warnings for HBV reactivation and PML.

key_facts.fact: The approval carried Breakthrough Therapy, Orphan Drug and Priority Review designations; no therapy had previously been approved by the FDA or EMA for the disease.
key_facts.excerpt: Regulatory momentum included Breakthrough Therapy, Orphan Drug, and Priority Review designations, addressing a PMN landscape previously lacking FDA/EMA-approved therapies

key_facts.fact: On the same day the FDA also approved AstraZeneca's Imfinzi plus Padcev before and after bladder removal for cisplatin-ineligible muscle-invasive bladder cancer, after the VOLGA trial showed a 42% lower risk of death versus surgery-based care.
key_facts.excerpt: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration on Friday, Nov. 13, approved AstraZeneca's Imfinzi with Padcev ... In the VOLGA trial, the pairing lowered the risk of death 42% compared with surgery-based care
